label: Simulated life: creatures, plants and characters follow simple seeded rules. They are not alive, aware or sentient.

realms.name: Aurelia · First Stratum
realms.blurb: Green isles where the Lux first fell.

realms.name: Verdant Deep · Second Stratum
realms.blurb: Forests so old the canopy has its own weather.

realms.name: Ember Reach · Third Stratum
realms.blurb: Red dunes and glassy crystal wastes.

realms.name: Luxfall · Seventh Stratum
realms.blurb: Floating highlands where light grows like grass.

field_net.text: Gently tag creatures for your bestiary (they are released at once).

sling.text: Fires pebbles to scare off predators. Nothing is hurt.

lux_staff.text: A make-believe glowing staff. Light it to make creatures keep their distance.

mossback.name: Mossback
mossback.blurb: Slow, round grazers covered in living moss.

duskwolf.name: Duskwolf
duskwolf.blurb: Shy night hunters that chase Mossbacks.

glowmoth.name: Glowmoth
glowmoth.blurb: Pollinators; flowers spread faster where they fly.

wardens.name: Wardens of the Wild
wardens.creed: Protect living things and their balance.

ilsa.name: Warden Ilsa
ilsa.persona: a calm, kind ranger who protects the Wildwood's creatures
greet: Mind your step, traveller. The moss is growing.
Back again? The Mossbacks remember you.
Friend of the Wild! Good to see you.

start.text: Duskwolves have been chasing the Mossbacks near the river. Some villagers want them driven off.

choices.label: Leave the wolves be. Predators keep the balance.
Scare the wolves away from the river.
Let's count them first, like a fair test.

balance.text: Wise. Without wolves, the Mossbacks would eat every flower. Watch the numbers rise and fall over the days.

scare.text: Fewer wolves, then. But watch the meadow. More grazers means fewer flowers.

count.text: Bring me a tally from the Wildwood. Numbers before opinions.

bram.name: Tinker Bram
bram.persona: an enthusiastic inventor who loves gadgets and safe experiments
greet: Mind the sparks! What do you need?
Partner! I've saved you the best workbench.

start.text: I want to build a lantern road through the Wildwood. More light, more travellers! What do you think?

choices.label: Only with dim lanterns, so the moths aren't confused.
Test one lantern first and measure what it changes.

build.text: Splendid! Bring crystal and wood and we'll light the way.

compromise.text: Dim lanterns, eh? Fewer lumens, happier moths. Clever.

test.text: A control and a variable! You'd make a fine Artificer AND a Lorekeeper.

oru.name: Sage Oru
oru.persona: a thoughtful scholar who loves evidence and labels speculation honestly
greet: Hmm? Ah, a visitor. Ask, and we shall test.

start.text: The four factions argue about the Lux Accord, the rule for sharing Aurelia. When you have spoken to Ilsa, Bram and Rook, return and we'll call the council.

strata.text: Oliver's SSR theory describes reality as layers built step by step from simple rules. It's his framework, not established science, so we test it rather than just believe it.

choices.label: Testing is the best way to learn.

council.text: The council meets. Your choices are weighed…

rook.name: Rook the Drifter
rook.persona: a cheerful wanderer who trades stories and values fairness
greet: Oi! Fancy a trade or a tale?
The road brought you back, eh?

start.text: Travellers are finding new strata past the edges of the map. Should maps be shared with everyone, or kept by the guilds?

choices.label: Share maps with everyone, for free.
Guilds keep them safe, but sell copies cheaply.
Record them in the Lorekeepers' library.

share.text: Ha! The open road for all. Here, take this tip: the far east is all crystal wastes.

guild.text: Hmph. Fair enough, as long as they stay cheap.

library.text: A library! Everyone can read, nobody can hoard. I like it.

accord.name: The Accord of Light
accord.text: Every faction trusts you. The Lux Accord is signed by all four, and Aurelia is shared fairly.

wardens.name: The Warden's Watch
wardens.text: The Wild comes first. The Wardens guard the balance and the forests thrive.

artificers.name: The Artificer Dawn
artificers.text: Lantern roads and workshops spread. Aurelia gets brighter and busier.

lorekeepers.name: The Age of Evidence
lorekeepers.text: Every claim is tested and recorded. The great library opens its doors.

drifters.name: The Open Road
drifters.text: Maps are free and roads are open. Travellers flood into new strata.

discovery.label_mystical: Symbolic, in-game only (MYSTICAL/IN-GAME): magic, spirits and astrology are make-believe parts of the game's story, never established science.

energy_transfer.gcse: energy is never made or destroyed, only transferred (e.g. chemical store to thermal store)

friction.gcse: friction is a force that opposes motion and turns kinetic energy into heat

photosynthesis.gcse: plants use light energy to turn carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen

refraction.gcse: light changes speed and bends when it passes from one material into another

natural_selection.gcse: individuals with helpful inherited traits survive and reproduce more, so traits spread over generations

pollination.gcse: pollinators carry pollen between flowers so plants can make seeds

insulation.gcse: insulators slow the rate of thermal energy transfer

lever.gcse: moment = force × distance from the pivot, so a long lever multiplies force

lens.gcse: a convex lens focuses light to make things look bigger or brighter

pulley.gcse: pulleys share a load between rope sections, so less force is needed over a longer distance

circuit.gcse: current flows round a complete circuit; V = I × R

kiln.gcse: heating clay or sand to high temperature changes its structure permanently

harmony.gcse: a symbolic idea in the story: everything in Aurelia fits together in layers

lux_sigil.gcse: a make-believe glyph from the legend of the Lux

ancestral_echo.gcse: a story symbol for remembering the creatures that came before

strata_resonance.gcse: a symbolic idea from Oliver's SSR theory: each layer echoes the one beneath (his framework, not established science)

ability.sense: reach +{m} (harvest, build and observe from further away)
ability.calm: creatures stay calm near you (+{m} calm)

structure.growth: plants in this stratum grow faster (+{m}×5%)
structure.light: predators hunt less near the light (calm +{m})

effects.effect: a consumable: {m} uses of double harvest
effects.ritual: symbolic blessing: Glowmoths spread flowers more (+{m}) and like-minded factions trust you more

canon.source: OmniLux Prime Doctrine, Masterpiece Edition (Nov 2026) with the SSR and CRA theses by Oliver Lux Prime Thorley

conservation.name: Conservation law
conservation.fact: Energy is conserved: it is transferred between stores, never created from nothing.
conservation.game: An invention's power (principle tiers × 2 + material values) may not exceed your invention budget.

stratum.name: Stratum ascent
stratum.theory: SSR (Thorley) describes reality as nine strata, M0 to M8 (with M∞ as a formal limit), each built from the one beneath; the CRA models this as a least fixed point reached step by step (31 of 33 atoms on the reference trace).
stratum.game: Each invention sits on a stratum (power ÷ 6, rounded down, M0 to M8). You may build at most one stratum above the highest you have reached.

harmonic.name: Harmonic involution
harmonic.fact: On the integers modulo 144, adding 72 twice returns every number to itself (an involution), and 144 = 2 × 72.
harmonic.theory: SSR reads the +72 involution on ℤ144 as a symmetry of the Lux lattice.
harmonic.game: If 72 × power is a whole number of 144-cycles (true when power is even), the invention is harmonic and gains +10 stability.

fair_test.name: Fair-test law
fair_test.fact: Repeating a trial many times shows whether a result is reliable: with success chance p in n trials, the expected count is np and the spread is √(np(1−p)) (binomial distribution).
fair_test.game: Every invention is tested in 144 seeded trials (a 1/1000 scale of the doctrine's 144,000-trial protocol); it works only if more than 72 succeed.

carrier.name: Finite carrier bound
carrier.fact: On a finite set, growth from one item by doubling can happen at most ⌊log₂|U|⌋ times: 17 times for 144,000 items. With a chosen doubling time of 12.32 years that is 209.44 years. Unbounded exponential growth is impossible on a finite set.
carrier.game: Each explorer can hold at most 144 inventions, and the budget grows by steps, never without limit.

half_life.name: Half-life law
half_life.fact: Tritium's half-life is 4500 ± 8 days (NIST), which is 12.32 years. After time t, the amount left is N = N₀ × 2^(−t/T½).
half_life.game: Each invention has an in-game half-life of 12.32 × (stratum + 1) days, which sets how long its glow (shown on its card) lasts.

year_clock.name: The year as a shared clock
year_clock.fact: 4500 ÷ 12.32 = 28,125/77 = 365.2597… days, which is just the days-per-year used in the conversion, slightly changed by rounding.
year_clock.theory: SSR (Thorley) reads the year as a stratum where cosmic time and human time share a clock. This is an interpretation, not a discovery.

binomial.plain: mean = n p,  spread σ = √(n p (1 − p))

friction_heat.plain: work done = force × distance (becomes heat through friction)

canon.no_proof: This card describes a game invention. Nothing here is a real-world experiment or proof. SSR/CRA THEORY statements are Oliver Lux Prime Thorley's framework, not established science.
